title: The Virtues of Sending Blessings
summary: Emphasizes the virtues of reciting blessings on the Prophet (PBUH) frequently, especially on Fridays, as it brings multiple divine blessings and favors.
translation: Every Muslim should make it a practice to frequently send blessings (Durood) upon the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) on Fridays. While there are many virtues of reciting Durood, there are even greater virtues associated with frequently sending blessings on Fridays, according to a narration from Anas (RA). The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) stated, "Send blessings on me abundantly on Fridays and the night preceding it." Whoever sends blessings on the Prophet once will receive tenfold mercy from Allah. The study of the Prophet’s sayings and the command in the Quran by Allah to send Durood upon the Prophet is emphasized, as in the verse: "Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings on the Prophet. O you who believe, send blessings on him and peace abundantly" (Surah Al-Ahzab, 33:56). The Companions, upon learning of this verse, asked the Prophet (PBUH) for guidance on how to send blessings, leading to the teaching of the Durood Ibrahim, which is recited during prayers. Sending blessings, even once in a lifetime, is an obligation on believers. The more one sends, the better, as it signifies faith and love for the Prophet (PBUH). No specific wording is mandated, but the Durood Ibrahim is most recommended. Frequent recitation of blessings is encouraged as means to express love for the Prophet, communicate devotion, and receive divine mercy. The narration includes the account of the Prophet smiling when informed by Angel Gabriel that each blessing sent would result in ten-fold mercy and safety from Allah. Narrations in Mishkat and Tafsir Qurtubi highlight the abundant rewards for sending blessings. Angels traverse the earth, carrying the greetings of followers to the Prophet, and among his followers, those frequent in sending blessings will be closest to him on the Day of Judgment.
